section.sectionSummaryBrief: Korach's error stemmed from his lack of self-nullification, which prevented him from grasping the synthesis of opposites in the firmament's separation.
section.t: And it may be said,
that the reason Korach erred and thought that the intent of the dividing firmament was the separation itself,
is,
because he did not possess the quality of self-nullification.
And the explanation is,
that this which was stated above
(section 3)
—that the intent in the lower waters being separated from the upper waters and descending below was so that they would have a yearning and thirst to ascend upward—
is a connection and inter-inclusion of two opposite attributes.
For from the perspective of the chassadim
(the advantage of revelations),
the superiority is in the upper waters, and there would be no need for the lower waters to be separated from the upper waters and descend below,
and from the perspective of the gevuros,
the superiority is in the revelation of the root of the lower waters themselves,
and there is no need for the lower waters to have a yearning and thirst to depart from their existence and ascend upward.
And that the intent in the descent of the lower waters below is that they should have a thirst to ascend upward—this is from the aspect of the Tiferes,
the central line,
which connects the opposites of Chessed and Gevurah,
so that the left is included in the right48.
And since the matter of inter-inclusion is from the aspect of self-nullification49,
therefore Korach, who lacked self-nullification,
this concept was not settled within him.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The service of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven" is achieved through self-nullification to fulfill the divine will, not for personal spiritual gratification.
section.t: And it may be said,
that similarly, regarding the service of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven,"
that even though one knows the great superiority of "in all your ways know Him"—
the knowledge of G‑dliness within worldly matters themselves—
nevertheless, all his engagement in worldly matters will be only as a means for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,
this is through self-nullification to fulfill the supernal will.
For since his service is not to quench his own thirst for a revelation of G‑dliness in his soul,
but rather he is surrendered and given over to fulfill the will of the Holy One, blessed be He,
therefore the revelation of knowing G‑dliness
(also)
in worldly matters is of no consequence to him,
and his entire desire is in the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,
the fulfillment of the will of the Holy One, blessed be He.
[And through this, he will also have the revelation of G‑dliness that is in worldly matters,
as explained above
(section 5),
that through the service of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven," one attains "in all your ways know Him."]

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The life that is above nature, accessed through self-nullification, enables one to engage in worldly matters for the sake of Heaven without stumbling.
section.t: And this is [the meaning of] "Hashem, our soul in life, and He did not give our foot to stumbling,"
for when a person engages in Torah and mitzvos, he is in the aspect of "head," and when he engages in worldly matters, he is in the aspect of "foot,"
and the power for this—that his feet
(his engagement in worldly matters)
will not stumble—
comes from the life in which "He placed our soul,"
the life that is above nature,
which is above the life of the soul itself,
even from the aspect of "chai be'etzem" (intrinsic life),
for from the level of the life of the soul itself
(including also the aspect of "chai be'etzem"),
it is possible that one will desire the revelation of G‑dliness within worldly matters,
and when his engagement in worldly matters is for the sake of
(the revelation within)
the worldly matters themselves,
and not for the sake of Heaven for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,
then his feet
(his involvement in matters of permission)
will stumble.
And in order that his feet not stumble,
so that his engagement in matters of permission is for the sake of Heaven as above,
this is through the life that is above nature
(and it may be said that the vessel for this is self-nullification),
for being above limitation, they connect the two opposites of Chessed and Gevurah,
so that even though one knows the superiority in the refinement of matters of permission,
nevertheless, his intent in doing matters of permission is for the sake of fulfilling Torah and mitzvos.
